# SYNTHBODY — Model Validation Report

**Software version** 0.1.0 · **Engine revision** `engine-2026.10.12b`
**Generated by** `backend/scripts/run_validation.py`
**Raw results** [docs/validation_results.json](docs/validation_results.json)

Every number in this document was produced by running the validation pipeline
against the shipped observed datasets. Nothing here is quoted from a
publication, estimated by hand, or carried over from a previous run. Re-run it
yourself:

```bash
cd backend && python scripts/run_validation.py
```

---

## 1. What "validated" means here, and what it does not

SYNTHBODY distinguishes five validation states and never upgrades one to make a
model look better supported:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `independently_validated` | Compared against observed data that was **not** used to estimate its parameters, within the population and design of that dataset only. |
| `calibrated_only` | Reproduces the dataset its own parameters were fitted to. Weak evidence: it shows the fit worked, not that the model generalises. |
| `structurally_verified` | Numerics verified against analytic solutions, limiting cases and mass balance. No comparison against clinical observations. |
| `research_only` | Implemented from published equations with traceable parameters, but no quantitative comparison against observed data. |
| `not_validated` | No validation of any kind. |

**None of these states means clinically validated.** SYNTHBODY has not been
reviewed by any regulator, has not been compared against a prospective clinical
study, and is not a medical device.

## 2. The protocol, fixed in advance

1. Split the dataset **by subject id**: odd-numbered subjects calibrate,
   even-numbered subjects are held out. The rule lives in
   `deterministic_split()` in code, so it cannot be chosen after seeing results.
2. Estimate typical parameters from the **calibration subjects only**, by
   two-stage fitting (per-subject weighted non-linear least squares, then
   geometric mean of the individual estimates).
3. Predict the **held-out subjects** using that single typical parameter vector,
   adjusted only by each held-out subject's own recorded dose and body weight.
   No held-out observation ever enters the estimation.
4. Report agreement statistics **separately** for calibration and held-out data.

Step 4 is the whole point. Calibration-set agreement is a software-correctness
check. Only the held-out numbers are evidence about the model.

---

## 3. Theophylline — one-compartment, first-order absorption

**Model** `pk_1cmt_foa` · **Dataset** `Theoph` (R `datasets`, GPL-2 | GPL-3)
**Design** 12 healthy adults, single oral dose (~300 mg), 11 samples over ~25 h
**Calibration subjects** 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 · **Held out** 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12

### Estimated typical parameters (calibration set only)

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Between-subject CV% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CL/F | 0.03791 | L/h/kg | 40.3 |
| V/F | 0.4588 | L/kg | 18.0 |
| ka | 2.133 | 1/h | 120.5 |

Bioavailability is not identifiable from oral-only data and was fixed at 1, so
CL and V are **apparent** values (CL/F, V/F).

### Independent corroboration (not used in the estimation)

Adult theophylline clearance is widely reported at approximately
**0.04 L/h/kg** and volume of distribution at approximately **0.5 L/kg**. The
estimator saw only the Theoph concentrations and landed at 0.0379 L/h/kg and
0.459 L/kg. That agreement is genuine out-of-sample corroboration of the
estimation machinery, and it is the strongest single piece of evidence in this
release.

### Agreement

| Statistic | Calibration (n=66) | **Held-out (n=66)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RMSE | 1.771 mg/L | **1.503 mg/L** |
| MAE | 1.282 mg/L | **1.052 mg/L** |
| Mean percent error | +14.4% | **+26.8%** |
| Median absolute percent error | 19.4% | **19.2%** |
| Average fold error (bias) | 1.070 | **1.209** |
| Absolute average fold error (precision) | 1.334 | **1.293** |
| Within 1.25-fold | 55.0% | **66.7%** |
| Within 1.5-fold | 81.7% | **83.3%** |
| Within 2-fold | 91.7% | **90.0%** |
| R² vs line of identity | 0.613 | **0.724** |
| Lin concordance | 0.808 | **0.864** |

### Honest reading

Typical precision on held-out subjects is about **29%** (AAFE 1.29), with a
**21% over-prediction bias** (AFE 1.21). 90% of held-out observations fall
within 2-fold. Median absolute percent error is 19%.

This is evidence for **single-dose oral theophylline in healthy adults over
about 25 hours, and nothing else.** It says nothing about intravenous dosing,
multiple dosing, children, the elderly, hepatic impairment, smokers or drug
interactions — all of which the software will happily let you simulate.

### Known problems the pipeline surfaces

- **Subject 1 cannot be fitted properly.** It has a non-zero concentration
  (0.74 mg/L) recorded at nominal time zero, which a model whose absorption
  depot starts empty cannot reproduce. Its individual estimates carry relative
  standard errors above 1400%. The pipeline reports this rather than averaging
  it away.
- **Subject 7** also returns relative standard errors above 300%.
- **ka is poorly determined.** A between-subject CV of 120% on an absorption
  rate constant means the sampling schedule does not resolve it. Absorption-phase
  predictions should be treated with corresponding scepticism.
- Six observations are excluded from fold-error statistics because an observed
  or predicted value is non-positive (concentrations recorded as 0 at t=0).

## 4. Indomethacin — two-compartment

**Model** `pk_2cmt` · **Dataset** `Indometh` (R `datasets`, GPL-2 | GPL-3)
**Design** 6 subjects, intravenous indomethacin, 11 samples over 8 h
**Calibration subjects** 1, 3, 5 · **Held out** 2, 4, 6

### Estimated typical parameters (calibration set only)

| Parameter | Value | Unit | Between-subject CV% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CL | 0.3413 | L/h per unit dose | 30.3 |
| V1 | 0.3432 | L per unit dose | 23.3 |
| Q | 0.2318 | L/h per unit dose | 47.8 |
| V2 | 0.9244 | L per unit dose | 3.55 |

> **The administered dose is absent from the distributed dataset.** SYNTHBODY
> uses a nominal dose of 1 unit, so every volume and clearance above is an
> apparent value *per unit dose*, not an absolute L or L/h. Rate constants and
> the distribution/elimination ratios derived from them remain valid; absolute
> volumes do not.

### Agreement

| Statistic | Calibration (n=33) | **Held-out (n=33)** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RMSE | 0.209 mg/L | **0.149 mg/L** |
| MAE | 0.127 mg/L | **0.117 mg/L** |
| Mean percent error | +5.55% | **−20.3%** |
| Median absolute percent error | 21.3% | **22.3%** |
| Average fold error (bias) | 1.023 | **0.772** |
| Absolute average fold error (precision) | 1.238 | **1.335** |
| Within 1.25-fold | 63.6% | **45.5%** |
| Within 1.5-fold | 84.8% | **78.8%** |
| Within 2-fold | 100% | **93.9%** |
| R² vs line of identity | 0.891 | **0.942** |
| Lin concordance | 0.941 | **0.970** |

### Honest reading

Typical precision on held-out subjects is about **33%** (AAFE 1.34), with a
**23% under-prediction bias** (AFE 0.77). 94% of held-out observations fall
within 2-fold.

The R² of 0.94 looks impressive and is partly an artefact: indomethacin
concentrations span more than an order of magnitude over 8 hours, so a model
that merely captures the shape of the decline scores well against the line of
identity. The AAFE and the 45% within-1.25-fold figure are the more informative
numbers.

### Known problems

- **Three calibration subjects.** The typical values and *especially* the
  variability estimates are very imprecise. The reported V2 CV of 3.55% is
  implausibly small for a peripheral volume and should not be read as evidence
  that V2 is conserved; it reflects three subjects, one of which had an 81%
  relative standard error on that parameter.
- **The source study reports enterohepatic recirculation.** A plain
  two-compartment model cannot produce secondary concentration peaks, so that
  mechanism appears as irreducible fit error.
- **Eight hours of sampling under-determines the terminal phase**, so the
  terminal rate constant and anything derived from it are weak.

## 5. PBPK model — structural check only

**Model** `pbpk_perfusion_limited` · **Status** `research_only`

The whole-body PBPK model has **not** been compared against any observed
concentration-time profile. What has been verified:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Flow balance closes (cardiac output = sum of modelled tissue flows) | ✅ exact by construction |
| Mass balance closes over 48 h | ✅ error < 1e-6 relative |
| Total drug conserved with clearance set to zero | ✅ within 1e-6 over 500 h |
| All drug eventually eliminated with clearance on | ✅ 300.0 mg recovered within 0.1% over 2000 h |
| Every tissue:plasma ratio converges to its predicted Kp at equilibrium | ✅ within 1e-4 for all 12 tissues |
| Hepatic clearance never exceeds hepatic blood flow | ✅ asymptotes to flow limit |
| Vss from the ODE equilibrium matches the independent analytic Vss | ✅ within 0.2% |
| Cardiac output physiologically plausible | ✅ 390.2 L/h = **6.5 L/min** |
| GFR physiologically plausible | ✅ ~119 mL/min |

### The one external quantitative check

Predicted steady-state volume of distribution for theophylline:

| | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Predicted Vss | 33.52 L = **0.4797 L/kg** |
| Widely reported adult value | ~0.5 L/kg |
| **Fold difference** | **1.04** |

This passes a 2-fold criterion comfortably. It is also **weak evidence**, and
the report says so for three reasons:

1. The log P input is PubChem's **XLogP3**, a *computed* descriptor, not an
   experimental measurement.
2. The fraction unbound (0.60) is **inferred** from the commonly quoted "~40%
   protein bound"; SYNTHBODY did not retrieve a primary measurement.
3. The comparison value of 0.5 L/kg was **not extracted from a primary
   publication that SYNTHBODY opened**.

One scalar agreement, from inferred inputs, against a recalled literature
value, **was** the full extent of external validation for this module. Section
5a records the concentration-time test that has since replaced it.

### What the PBPK model's output must not be used for

Tissue concentrations are model output, not exposure predictions. In particular
**brain concentrations will be overestimated** for any compound actively
excluded from the CNS, because no blood-brain barrier is modelled.

---

## 5a. Oral PBPK - concentration-time validation

**Model** `pbpk_oral_acat` - **Status** `research_only` - Runs live at
`GET /api/validation/pbpk/oral-concentration-time`, and in the Evidence
workspace under **Oral PBPK validation**.

Section 5 recorded that the PBPK module had never been compared against an
observed concentration-time profile. This is that comparison. It became
possible only once the seven-compartment absorption model existed, because a
whole-body distribution model cannot predict an *oral* profile without a
mechanistic account of how the drug gets in.

### What was predicted a priori and what was calibrated

This distinction is the whole result. A validation that quietly fits the thing
it is measuring says nothing.

| Process | Status | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Distribution** | predicted a priori | All twelve tissue:plasma partition coefficients, and therefore the volume of distribution, from Poulin-Theil on log P, fu and B:P. **Never fitted.** |
| **Absorption** | predicted a priori | Gastric emptying, transit, dissolution and permeability-limited uptake from shipped GI physiology at the **pre-specified** Peff of 3.0e-4 cm/s. There is no ka to estimate. |
| **Elimination** | calibrated out-of-sample | One number - CL/kg from the **calibration** subjects - inverted through the well-stirred model to a hepatic CLint. Evaluated on different subjects. |

Two of the three processes that shape an oral profile are predicted from
physicochemistry; one is calibrated on subjects disjoint from those evaluated.
The protocol is the same deterministic odd/even split used everywhere else in
SYNTHBODY, fixed in code so it cannot be chosen after seeing results.

Calibration subjects 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 - held out 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 -
calibrated CL = 0.037907 L/h/kg.

### Agreement, 66 held-out observed concentrations

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| AAFE | **1.185** |
| AFE | 0.984 (very slight under-prediction) |
| Within 2-fold | **96.7%** (64/66) |
| Within 1.5-fold | 95.0% |
| Median absolute error | **14.4%** |
| RMSE | 1.004 mg/L |
| R-squared vs line of identity | 0.877 |
| Lin's concordance | 0.930 |

| Exposure metric | AAFE | AFE | Within 2-fold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AUC | 1.134 | 1.061 | 100% |
| Cmax | 1.099 | 0.918 | 100% |
| tmax | 1.521 | 1.115 | 83% |

### The volume of distribution was never fitted

| | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Predicted from physicochemistry (Poulin-Theil) | **0.479 L/kg** |
| Fitted by the empirical model from calibration data | 0.459 L/kg |
| **Fold difference** | **1.04** |

This is a materially stronger claim than section 5's scalar check. There, a
predicted Vss was compared against a recalled literature value. Here the same
predicted Vss is load-bearing inside a dynamic model whose output is compared
point by point against observed concentrations - so an error in it would show
up as a systematic distortion of the curve, not merely as a number that happens
to look right.

### Compared with the empirical one-compartment model

| | Empirical 1-cmt | Oral PBPK |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parameters estimated from this drug | **3** (CL, V, ka) | **1** (CL) |
| Volume of distribution | fitted | predicted |
| Absorption rate | fitted | predicted |
| Held-out AAFE | 1.293 | **1.185** |
| Held-out within 2-fold | 90% | **96.7%** |

The PBPK model is more accurate on held-out data while estimating two fewer
parameters from it. **This is not a like-for-like contest** and the software
says so wherever it reports the comparison: the two models were given different
amounts of information about theophylline. Equal accuracy at fewer degrees of
freedom would already have been the meaningful result. Lower error is a stronger
one, but what matters is the degrees of freedom, not the decimal.

### Honest reading

**What this establishes.** For a freely soluble, highly permeable, neutral,
low-extraction, minimally bound drug, SYNTHBODY can predict an observed human
oral plasma profile from physicochemistry plus one calibrated clearance, to
within about 15% median error. The mechanistic chain - dissolution, transit,
permeability, portal absorption, first pass, tissue partitioning, well-stirred
clearance - composes without an empirical correction factor anywhere in it.

**What it does not establish.**

1. **One drug, one study, one population.** Twelve healthy adults, single oral
   dose. Theophylline is close to the easiest case a PBPK model can be given.
   Nothing here transfers to poorly soluble, highly bound, high-extraction or
   basic drugs - and Poulin-Theil is specifically known to predict badly for
   moderate-to-strong bases.
2. **AUC is the weak metric.** Clearance was calibrated, and AUC is
   approximately dose x F / CL. Judge this on curve shape, Cmax and tmax.
3. **Out-of-sample across subjects is not out-of-sample across studies.** The
   six held-out subjects came from the same study, protocol and laboratory as
   the six used for calibration.
4. **Every tissue concentration remains unvalidated.** This tests the plasma
   prediction only. No observed human tissue concentration data ships with
   SYNTHBODY. Plasma agreement does not establish that any individual organ
   compartment is right, and the model's tissue outputs are labelled
   UNVALIDATED in the UI for that reason.

### The weakness the test exposed

tmax is the worst metric (AAFE 1.521, only 83% within 2-fold), and the
per-subject numbers show exactly why:

| Subject | Observed tmax | Predicted tmax |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 1.92 h | 2.18 h |
| 4 | 1.07 h | 2.21 h |
| 6 | 1.15 h | 2.19 h |
| 8 | 2.02 h | 2.21 h |
| 10 | 3.55 h | 2.22 h |
| 12 | 3.52 h | 2.21 h |

Observed tmax spans 1.07-3.55 h. Predicted tmax spans 2.18-2.22 h. The model
gives every subject essentially the same absorption profile, because gastric
emptying is a fixed population constant with no between-subject variability.
The prediction sits near the middle of the observed spread - which is why AFE
is a respectable 1.115 while AAFE is poor - but it cannot reproduce the spread
itself. Fixing this needs a distribution on gastric emptying rate, tracked in
PROGRESS.md as a prerequisite for the population absorption work.

### Reproducing it

Every figure above is pinned by `tests/test_oral_pbpk.py`, which compares
against `tests/baseline/oral_pbpk_validation.json` - a fixture generated by
running the protocol, never typed by hand. To regenerate the numbers directly,
call `run_oral_pbpk_validation()` from
`synthbody.engine.analysis.pbpk_validation`, or hit the API endpoint above.

## 6. Michaelis-Menten model — structurally verified only

**Model** `pk_1cmt_mm` · **Status** `structurally_verified`

Verified:

- Reduces to first-order kinetics with CL = Vmax/Km when C ≪ Km (agreement
  better than 1e-4 of peak against the analytic monoexponential).
- Shows supra-proportional exposure above Km (doubling a 500 mg dose increases
  AUC by more than 2.05×).
- Analytic Jacobian matches central finite differences to 1e-5.
- Mass balance closes to better than 1e-7.
- An infusion rate above Vmax produces unbounded accumulation with no plateau,
  while a linear model with CL = Vmax/Km would have reached steady state.

**No observed-data validation exists.** SYNTHBODY ships no licensed non-linear
pharmacokinetic dataset. The only compound using this model is an explicitly
synthetic demonstration compound whose every parameter is invented.

---

## 7. Pharmacodynamic models — research only

Three standard structures are implemented (sigmoid Emax, indirect response in
all four Dayneka-Garg-Jusko variants, effect compartment) and numerically
verified: baseline is stationary at R0 = kin/kout, the response returns to
baseline after washout, and effect-site concentration converges to plasma
concentration at steady state.

**Every pharmacodynamic parameter shipped is `illustrative`.** SYNTHBODY ships
no pharmacodynamic dataset and did not extract concentration-effect values from
any publication. The theophylline Emax curve demonstrates that the PK/PD
machinery works; it is not a prediction of bronchodilator response.

---

## 8. Numerical verification of the engine itself

Separate from clinical validation, the solver is verified against closed-form
solutions. From the automated suite (199 tests, all passing):

| Verification | Result |
| --- | --- |
| One-compartment ODE vs Bateman analytic solution | agreement < 1e-8 of peak |
| Two-compartment ODE vs biexponential analytic solution | agreement < 1e-8 of peak |
| All five solvers (LSODA, BDF, Radau, RK45, DOP853) vs analytic | agreement < 1e-7 of peak |
| Hybrid rate constants satisfy the characteristic polynomial | exact to 1e-12 |
| Superposition holds for linear models (2 doses = sum of 2 single doses) | < 1e-8 of peak |
| Dose proportionality for linear models | 1e-7 relative |
| Infusion steady state = R0/CL | 1e-6 relative |
| Concentration at one half-life into an infusion = 50% of Css | 1e-6 absolute |
| Steady-state Cmax and Cmin vs multiple-dose closed form (40 doses) | 1e-6 and 1e-5 relative |
| Peak-to-trough difference equals exactly one dose / V | 1e-5 relative |
| ka = ke removable singularity handled without blow-up | finite, < 1e-7 |
| Analytic Jacobians vs central finite differences | 1e-5 relative |
| Mass balance (all models) | < 1e-9 at tight tolerance |
| Tolerance-convergence self-check detects deliberately loose tolerances | ✅ |
| Local sensitivity recovers exact analytic derivatives (AUC = D/CL → −1) | 1e-5 relative |
| Sobol first-order indices sum to 1 for an additive model | within 0.08 |
| Sobol detects pure interaction for a multiplicative model | ST − S1 > 0.5 |
| Population sampler recovers requested CV% and correlation | within 5% and 0.03 |
| Estimator recovers known parameters from noise-free data | 0.1% relative |
| Reproduction of a stored run | bitwise identical, hash matches |

## 9. What would be needed to go further

| To claim | You would need |
| --- | --- |
| Validated intravenous theophylline PK | A licensed IV theophylline dataset. Then F becomes identifiable and CL/V stop being apparent values. |
| Validated multiple-dose PK | A licensed multiple-dose dataset. Accumulation and any time-varying clearance are currently unvalidated extrapolation. |
| Validated population variability | Non-linear mixed-effects estimation (FOCE or SAEM). Two-stage fitting gives an upper bound, not an estimate. |
| Validated covariate effects | A dataset stratified by the covariate. The hepatic and smoking multipliers here are direction-only. |
| Validated PBPK | Observed concentration-time data for a compound with measured log P, fu and B:P, plus Rodgers-Rowland partitioning for ionisable compounds. |
| Validated pharmacodynamics | Paired concentration-and-effect measurements. Nothing less will identify ke0, EC50 or turnover parameters. |
| Any clinical claim | Prospective comparison against clinical outcomes, a quality system, and regulatory engagement. Not a software task. |

---

## 10. Reproducing this report

```bash
cd backend
python -m pytest tests/ -q               # 199 tests
python scripts/run_validation.py         # the numbers above
python scripts/run_validation.py --json out.json
```

The validation pipeline runs live in the application too: open the **Evidence**
workspace → *Model validation*. It re-fits and re-predicts on every request, so
the figures shown are always current for the code you are running rather than a
cached claim.
